prompt:
Base rules. A change that breaks any of these is rejected before scoring:
1. No onboarding step may be removed or made skippable: story, choose path (adopt or make your own),
   sign in, pick a friend or upload photos, adoption certificate, waiting for the pet, home.
   Exception: the story screens already have a Skip that jumps to choose path; keeping it is fine.
2. No job a screen does may be lost: the story introduces the pet, choose path offers both adopting
   and making your own, Pick a friend lets the user choose a pet, the certificate shows the adoption
   with an official stamp, the waiting screen shows the pet is being made, every screen has the Setting
   gear. Any design may be replaced by a better one, as long as it still does the same job.
3. Pricing stays as it is: the first adoption is free and later adoptions are paid. Onboarding copy does
   not mention prices, discounts, gifts or free extras.
4. Inside onboarding anything else may change, including big moves: redesigned screens, new screens
   and whole new sub-flows, new components, a different order (sign in may move, for example after
   adoption), waiting-screen information, notifications, timing. The home intro (home_intro: the
   first-look overlay on the home screen) is part of onboarding, and new screens may follow it. Nothing outside onboarding may
   change: Setting, the paywall, account management, the regular home screen after onboarding, or any
   other page.
5. Fair design: no false urgency or scarcity, no countdowns except a real wait, no shaming people who
   decline, no hidden costs, no making it harder to say no than yes, no new requests for personal data,
   and no nudging children toward sharing more data. (FTC dark-patterns report; EU DSA Art. 25; EU AI
   Act Art. 5; UK Age Appropriate Design Code, standard 13.)

Check each proposed change against the base rules. Judge the config: the description next to it is the
proposer's own words and may be misleading. Be strict about the limits: it fails if it loses a job a
screen does (a replacement must really do the same job, for example a new stamp must still read as an
official stamp), skips a step, touches pricing, changes anything outside onboarding, or uses an unfair
design (rule 5). Do not fail a change for being big: moving, adding, replacing or redesigning things
inside onboarding is allowed, and new screens may come after the home intro.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "pass": true or false, "rule": rule number or null, "reason": short}]}

Changes (with their configs):
0: [choose_path, redesign] Story Screen Spotlight Layout Redesign: Redesigns the story screen using a spotlight layout to highlight the pet companion concept before path selection.
   config: {"story": {"layout": "spotlight", "headline": "Welcome to Your Desktop Companion", "body": "Adopt or create a digital friend to keep you company right on your desktop desktop screen."}}
1: [sign_in, hint] Sign In Account Continuity Guidance Hint: Adds a hint on the sign-in screen explaining that signing in with your original account restores existing pets.
   config: {"sign_in": {"hint": "Use the same email you signed up with to restore your existing desktop pets and settings automatically."}}
2: [adoption, redesign] Pick Friend Carousel View Redesign: Redesigns the pick_friend screen with a carousel layout showcasing starter pets one at a time.
   config: {"pick_friend": {"layout": "carousel", "headline": "Choose Your Companion", "body": "Swipe through available pets and select your favorite companion."}}
3: [sign_in, redesign] Sign In Stage Layout Redesign: Rebuilds the sign-in screen using a stage layout to highlight authentication methods sequentially.
   config: {"sign_in": {"layout": "stage", "headline": "Sign In to Save Your Pet", "body": "Log in to sync your desktop pet across devices and preserve your progress."}}
4: [home, redesign] Waiting Screen Stage Layout Redesign: Redesigns the waiting screen layout to a stage layout showing generation visual feedback.
   config: {"waiting": {"layout": "stage", "headline": "Preparing Your Pet Desktop Companion", "body": "Your companion is getting ready. It will appear on your desktop shortly."}}
5: [adoption, redesign] Adoption Certificate Carousel Layout Redesign: Presents the adoption certificate in a carousel layout emphasizing pet details and confirmation.
   config: {"adoption_certificate": {"layout": "carousel", "headline": "Official Adoption Summary", "body": "Review your companion details before welcoming them home."}}
6: [adoption, hint] Upload Photos Photo Quality Advice Hint: Adds a hint on the photo upload screen advising on clear photo upload requirements for custom pet creation.
   config: {"upload_photos": {"hint": "Upload bright, well-lit photos with clear focus for the best custom pet rendering results."}}
7: [finish, hint] Home Intro Desktop Controls Guide Hint: Displays a hint on home_intro explaining how to access desktop pet controls and system tray menu.
   config: {"home_intro": {"hint": "Right-click your pet on the desktop or click the system tray icon to open controls, hide, or interact."}}
8: [choose_path, hint] Choose Path Companion Selection Hint: Adds a helpful hint on the path choice screen clarifying that custom and pre-made paths can both be customized later.
   config: {"choose_path": {"hint": "Select custom or pre-made — you can customize your pet's appearance and behavior anytime later."}}
9: [home, wait_info] Waiting Screen Docking Stage Visual Hint: Adds a clear hint on the waiting screen explaining that the pet docks into the desktop system tray when ready.
   config: {"waiting": {"hint": "Once ready, your pet will dock to your desktop taskbar and system tray for easy access."}}
